chi_square.unit: terminology row; RxCUI repeated (independence assumption not strictly met)

lexical_coherence.metric: average Jaccard token overlap versus first name within each RxCUI (up to 15 terms), not clinical equivalence

not_applicable.reason: SAB has just one category in source; association undefined
All records have same QC label; association undefined
RxNorm columns are terminology identifiers/text, not multiple items measuring one latent construct

not_applicable.test: Normality test / one-sample t-test of RxCUI
not_applicable.reason: RxCUI is an identifier, not a quantitative outcome

interpretation_notes: All results are descriptive or exploratory for an observed source snapshot, not experiments or cause-effect evidence.
Welch compares independent RxCUI after excluding concepts shared across the two TTY labels; p-values Holm-adjusted across three planned contrasts.
Chi-square involves multiple names for the same RxCUI and violates strict observation independence. Treat p-values as diagnostic only; prioritize Cramer's V.
Extremely large sample sizes can yield very small p-values for negligible effect sizes.
Distinct TTY count and term count are arithmetically related: a high correlation is partly mechanical, not a novel clinical finding.
Lexical Jaccard measures text overlap, not synonym truth, therapeutic equivalence or clinical correctness.
No distribution normality or independence is guaranteed. No time-series tests on a single snapshot.

report_4_statistics.grain: RxNorm terminology row, not a clinical product or longitudinal record
report_4_statistics.population_statistics: population variance and SD (ddof=0) of this available RxNorm snapshot

mapping_handoff.note: RxNorm current prescribable terminology is not all RxNorm, nor does text parsing provide official RXNREL evidence
